text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SYNTHICHECK FAILURE eu-west-1 / canary-probe-3 — 5 consecutive failures. metric: failed_checks=5, median_latency=1350ms, p95=2400ms. Runbook: https://redwood.runbooks/synth-failure. Creating PagerDuty incident PD-9144.

pagerduty-bot: PD-9144 fired -> Escalation policy: production-synth. Notifying: @tayla (primary), @simon (secondary). Link: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-9144

tayla (oncall): ack. joining console now. Starting quick blast radius check.

tayla (oncall): observed canary failures all point to 502 / connection-reset-from-upstream. Prober logs show repeated TCP resets to eu-nat cluster nodes.

simon: i'm seeing a spike in ephemeral port usage on eu-nat-1 and eu-nat-2 around 11:03 UTC. netstat shows many TIME_WAIT entries and port exhaustion warnings in kernel logs.

ravi: FYI I rolled an autosync change for prober-concurrency at 11:01 (short rollout). PR: https://github.com/redwood/prober-config/PR/445 — autosync now sets concurrency=50 for variant=v3 when stable=false. That might match the timeline.

tayla (oncall): command run: `kubectl -n infra logs deploy/canary-prober-eu-3 --tail=150` ->
```
I2026-03-14T11:02:59Z probe: starting seq=98 target=/embeddings
E2026-03-14T11:03:04Z probe: upstream connection reset by peer
E2026-03-14T11:03:05Z prober: error dialing backend: resource temporarily unavailable
I2026-03-14T11:03:06Z prober: concurrency set to 50 (autosync)
```

ops-bot: Executed: `kubectl -n infra scale deployment canary-prober-eu-3 --replicas=0` (by tayla) to stop probes temporarily while investigating.

cs-bot: Notified CS rotation: possible customer-visible increase in 5xx in EU region between 11:03-11:08 UTC. Impact: small subset (~0.3%) of API requests degraded. Suggested message draft queued.

tayla (oncall): immediate mitigation: paused autosync for prober and set concurrency=10. `kubectl -n infra set env deploy/canary-prober-eu PROBER_CONCURRENCY=10` and restarted deployment.

ops-bot: Executed: set env PROBER_CONCURRENCY=10 on canary-prober-eu (by tayla). Restarted pods.

simon: after reducing concurrency, ephemeral port usage dropped and connection resets ceased. p95 latency from 2400ms -> 320ms within 2 minutes.

ravi: rolling back the autosync change now and opening a guardrail: limit concurrency max 20 and add randomized jitter on prober start to avoid synchronized bursts. PR: https://github.com/redwood/prober-config/PR/446 (draft).

cs-bot: CS message sent to affected tenants: "We observed transient elevated error rates for a small subset of requests in EU region. We applied mitigation; no customer action required."

tayla (oncall): PD-9144 acknowledged at 11:12 UTC. I'll keep watch for 20 minutes then close if stable. Adding temporary suppression for canary flapping alerts for 15m to avoid noise while guardrails land.

simon: digging root cause: sequence = autosync bumped concurrency at scale during a canary rollout; backpressure on NAT boxes caused ephemeral port exhaustion because probes open many short-lived connections without reuse. RCE: autosync should've honored max-concurrency guard and connection pooling.

ravi: adding unit/integration test to CI: autosync must not set concurrency > 20 and we will add e2e that simulates 1-min rollout at high qps. Also schedule a follow-up to migrate probes to use HTTP keepalive connection pooling.

tayla (oncall): monitoring shows EU host metrics normalized; p95 and error-rate stable. No large customer incidents found in CS logs.

pagerduty-bot: PD-9144 resolved (mitigated) by tayla at 11:20 UTC.

incident-bot: PD-9144 closed. Artifacts: prober logs, nat kernel logs, kube events, autosync PRs (PR/445, PR/446). Postmortem assigned to ravi.

tayla (oncall): next steps: 1) merge guardrail PR, 2) add concurrency assertion to autosync CI, 3) implement keepalive in prober SDK, 4) run canary chaos test for NAT exhaustion scenarios. Owning: ravi (postmortem), simon (nat capacity assessment).

ravi: will draft postmortem and include timeline, mitigating commands, and follow-ups. tagging @simon for NAT sizing numbers.

simon: will run thru NAT port headroom and propose incremental capacity + monitoring for ephemeral port saturation.

tayla (oncall): filing short summary in #postmortems in ~1h. thanks for fast response everyone :thumbsup:
